common_name: Empress of India Nasturtium (Dark Red Blue-Green Foliage Nasturtium)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Empress of India is a classic heirloom nasturtium prized for deep crimson-red flowers held above distinctive blue-green foliage, a striking color combination unlike the more common orange-flowered, green-leaved types.

directions: Direct sow in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; rich soil produces excess foliage at the expense of flowers. Empress of India is a beloved heirloom nasturtium dating to the Victorian era, valued for its striking combination of deep, velvety crimson-red flowers set against distinctive blue-green, rounded leaves, a more refined and dramatic look than the typical bright orange-and-green nasturtium. Both the peppery flowers and leaves are edible, adding a colorful, spicy accent to salads, and the compact, mounding habit suits containers, edging, and small garden spaces. It blooms continuously through the growing season with essentially no care beyond occasional watering during dry spells, and self-seeds readily if seed pods are left to mature.

common_name: Jewel Mix Nasturtium (Classic Mixed-Color Compact Nasturtium)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Jewel Mix is a classic compact, mounding (non-vining) nasturtium blend producing a full range of warm flower colors from cream through gold, orange, and deep red.

directions: Direct sow in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; overly fertile soil produces lush leaves at the expense of flowers. Jewel Mix is one of the most classic and widely grown nasturtium blends, producing compact, bushy plants (rather than the long trailing vines of climbing types) covered in semi-double flowers spanning cream, yellow, gold, orange, salmon, and deep red, all with the same cheerful, informal charm nasturtiums are known for. Both flowers and round leaves are edible with a peppery, watercress-like bite, making them a popular addition to salads and as an edible garnish. The compact habit suits containers, edging, and small beds, and plants bloom continuously from early summer through frost with minimal care.

common_name: Sunburst Scallop Squash (Bright Yellow AAS-Winning Patty Pan Squash)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost when soil is warm; Sunburst is an AAS-winning hybrid patty pan squash producing bright golden-yellow, scalloped, saucer-shaped fruit best picked small and tender.

directions: Direct sow in warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Sunburst is a widely grown hybrid patty pan (scallop) squash producing cheerful, bright golden-yellow, saucer-shaped fruit with the classic scalloped edge, best harvested small, at two to three inches across, when the skin is tender and the flavor is sweetest. Picking regularly, every day or two during peak season, keeps the compact, bushy plants productive over a long summer harvest and prevents fruit from becoming tough and seedy. Like other summer squash it is a heavy producer and benefits from consistent moisture and monitoring for squash vine borer and squash bugs, common pests in Gulf South gardens.
